when: GET /api/help. How-do-I tiles. Not sent to a model.
title: Help

items.h: How do I tag a company or a person?

blocks.p: Three prefixes. Type one and a menu opens. You can chain slash bounds in one question.

ul: #ACME — pick a company. Home chat only. Inside a book, chat already knows the company — # does not list other books.
/people bob and /ticket ACME-12 — bound the question (search for, not talk to). Chain them: “what was /people bob response to /ticket ACME-12?”
@bob — talk to that person (address / send). Not how you search the book.
Type # to pick a company.
Type / to bound with /people or /ticket (and the other slash types).
Type @ when you mean to address someone.
The thread stays on that book. Do not point at another company.
Type /people or /ticket in chat to bound. The menu lists people and tickets on this book.
Book Search (far left) uses the same slash: /people bob, /ticket ACME-12, /email, /chat.

items.h: How do I add a company?

blocks.p: Settings → Add company opens a seven-stop train. Edit company stays one sheet. Fields marked * are required. Tip buttons explain each field.

ul: Role — Brand new (you own it, no handoff), View only (Manager / CSM / Rep), Takeover, or Covering (temp co-owner). Takeover and covering need the other person’s email. Covering needs an until date.
Book — name, slug (permanent), abbr, color, optional logo. Placeholders use Acme Inc.
Customer domain(s) — email domains (acme.com). That is how mail and calendar attach. Not a people list.
Feeds — tiles for IMAP, Gmail, Microsoft 365, Jira, Slack, Teams, Salesforce, Google Calendar, M365 Calendar. Tick what should fill this book. Finish only pulls feeds that are already live.

Look back — 14, 90, or 365 days for mail and calendar. This is the first-pull window in YOUR mailbox, not a dump of the whole account. Cap 200 messages. Auto-refresh every N minutes (default 5) keeps new mail and meetings coming after that.

People — mine customer people from mail, meetings, tickets, Slack, and Teams, de-duped by email. Last, First and first.last@domain become a name. Title, group, phone, and job description when those feeds have them. You tick who to add after Finish.

Attach — Finish saves the book, pulls the ticked live feeds, then shows a processing report (emails, meetings, tickets, Slack, people). You can add or fix a domain (acme.co.uk, or a typo like accme.com) and reprocess one feed or all of them, then tick people to add.
Open a former CSM’s mailbox. Pull is always your Google account.
Rewrite task To:Me on covering. Takeover stores that you own the book.
Resend calendar invites as you.

items.h: How do I find the project owner?

ul: Open the company (Home → Companies, or the breadcrumb).
Click the projects tab.
The owner is on the row, after the project type.
Search the project name if the list is long. Click the row to see the full owner picker.

blocks.p: On the right, ask: “Who owns Warehouse scan rollout on #ACME?” On Home, type # to pick the company. Inside a book, skip # — type @ if you need a person.

items.h: Which ticket has the highest priority?

ul: Open the book → tickets.
Each row shows priority · status on the right (Highest / High / Medium / Low, or P1–P4 from Jira).
Type /ticket in Search, then a key or word, for example /ticket P1 or /ticket ACME-12.

blocks.p: “Which ticket has the highest priority on #ACME?” Chat only uses tickets that are already in this desk — it does not invent keys.

items.h: What tasks are due this week?

ul: Stay on Home → Agenda.
In New mail / chat / tasks, open Filter and tick Tasks.
Rows with a due date show it in amber. Scan this week’s dates.

blocks.p: “What tasks are due this week?” or “What is due on #NWIN?” A task is a mail to yourself, not a Jira ticket.

items.h: How do I assign a task to someone else?

blocks.p: A task is still your mail. There is no separate assignee field. CC the person so they get a copy.

ul: On Agenda, click + in New mail / chat / tasks (or Compose → treat it as a task).
Pick the company. Name the task.
In CC, add people from that book (Tagify chips). They are the people who should act.
Set When Due By in the body. AI Suggest can fill name, due, CC, and note from the book.
Save draft or Send. Send asks you to confirm when SMTP is live.

items.h: How do I look through emails that are in draft only?

blocks.p: Save draft writes the message to Gmail Drafts when Google is connected with compose access. The desk also keeps a copy on that book. There is no Drafts folder on the email tab yet.

ul: Save draft — Gmail Drafts if Sign in with Google allowed sending and composing; otherwise the desk copy only.
Open Gmail → Drafts to keep editing there. Send from the desk removes that Gmail draft.
The email tab lists threads (sent and received), not unsent drafts.

items.h: How do I auto-draft replies into Gmail Drafts?

blocks.p: Per company. When AI Suggest Response to Draft is on, new mail with you on To: gets a Grok reply from that book’s tickets, Slack/Teams, people, past mail, and your intent, then lands in Gmail Drafts. You still Send.

ul: Settings → Companies → Edit the book.
Turn on AI Suggest Response to Draft. Save.
Sign in with Google must allow composing (Gmail Drafts). Send-only is not enough.
New inbound To: you is drafted on the next Gmail refresh. Turning it on also backfills recent matching mail (capped).
Open Gmail → Drafts, edit, or Send from the desk. Mail only on Cc/Bcc is skipped.

items.h: How do I search for an old chat on a ticket?

ul: Open the book.
In Search, type /chat and the ticket key, for example /chat ACME-12.
Or /slack ACME-12 or /teams ACME-12 — Slack and Teams share the slack / teams tab.

blocks.p: Open timeline and look for Slack or Teams thumbs near that ticket’s time. Use Past 7 / Past 30 if it is older than the default window.
“Find Slack about ACME-12 on #ACME.”

items.h: What's on fire this morning?

ul: Agenda: red Now line plus unread mail, Slack, Teams, and amber-due tasks.
Companies: tiles show health (watch / at risk / critical), open P1s, and the next meeting.
Click a tile that looks bad. The book opens on timeline around Now.

blocks.p: On Home chat (no book open): “What is on fire at #ACME?” or “What tasks are due this week?” Chat only names tickets and people already on this desk.

items.h: Did they reply to my last email?

ul: Open the company → email.
Open the thread. Newest message is last.
Or timeline: look for inbound mail (down) after your outbound (up).

blocks.p: With the book open, type /people and pick: “Did /people bob reply to my last email?” On Home, add #ACME. Chat answers yes/no from timestamps. It does not send a nudge.

items.h: How do I keep one company's mail off another book?

blocks.p: Books split on domains and connector tags, not on the subject line. ACME mail must not land on Northwind.

ul: Settings → Companies → Edit that book.
Domains: acme.com, acme.co.uk — inbound From/To those domains join this book.
Slack / Teams / Jira / Salesforce tags on the same screen pin chat and tickets.
Open the card. Color chip and abbreviation must match the company you meant.
Fix domains on Edit company, then Refresh health. Do not forward the mail to “fix” it.

items.h: How do I use this desk?

blocks.p: This is a local Customer Success Manager desk. One operator, many customer books. Tickets, mail, Slack, Teams, Salesforce, and calendar sit on one account so you do not reply to the wrong company.

ul: Home → Agenda for today.
Companies to open a book.
Tabs on the book for tickets, email, slack / teams, projects, people.
Desk chat on the right — # picks a company on Home. Inside a book, /people and /ticket bound the question. @ talks to someone.

items.h: How do I start my morning?

ul: Home → Agenda. The red line is Now. Meetings for today are on the left.
On the right, scan New mail / chat / tasks. Me / Us / Them tells you who the row is to.
Home → Companies if you need health and next meeting on every book at once.
Open the first book you owe. Timeline around Now is the story; tickets and email are the proof.
Ask chat after the book is open, or on Home type # to pick the company so it does not guess.

items.h: What will this desk not do?

ul: It will not send mail, Slack, Teams, or a calendar invite until you confirm Send (SMTP must be on).
Chat never invents ticket keys, meeting times, or people who are not on the book.
There is no Drafts folder on the email tab. Save draft keeps a copy on that book and, when Google allows it, in Gmail Drafts.
This is not a second Salesforce. Opportunities and cases that are already synced show on the Salesforce tab.
Keys and the database stay on this machine. There is no login on the desk itself.

items.h: How do I tell companies apart?

ul: Every book has a color chip and a 2–6 character abbreviation (ACME, NWIN, GLX).
They follow every row, tile, and chat so books never mix. In chat that abbreviation is #ACME.
Set color and logo under Settings → Companies → Edit.

items.h: How do I search this Help page?

ul: The box at the top filters How-do-I tiles as you type.
Typos are fine — timezome still finds timezones. Matching words highlight.
Chips under the box jump to a group. Clear the box to see every tile again.

items.h: How do I prep for my next meeting?

ul: Click the next meeting card (logo on the left, minutes on the right).
The lightbox is that event. Note who is on it.
Open the book from the chip or breadcrumb.
Timeline around Now — last mail, Slack, and tickets before the call.
People / org chart if you need who reports to whom.
World clock (the digital clock) if they are not in your timezone.

blocks.p: “What should I know before the QBR on #ACME?” It only uses this book. It will not put an invite on the calendar.

items.h: How do I follow up after a call?

ul: Open the meeting or the ticket you just discussed.
Notes at the bottom of the lightbox — what you promised, in your words. Save note.
If you owe mail: Compose or Reply. AI Suggest can draft from the book. Save draft or Send (confirm).
If you owe yourself work: Agenda → + for a task. CC the customer if they should see it.
Assign the mail or ticket to the project so it stays on that work, not just the company.

items.h: How do I get ready for a QBR?

ul: Open the book. Timeline Past 30 / Next 30 around Now.
Tickets: open P1s and anything still waiting.
Projects: status and owner. Blocked is the one to say out loud.
Email / slack / teams: last customer line vs last us line.
Ask chat: “QBR topics and wins on #ACME last 90 days.” It lists keys already on the book — it does not write slides.

items.h: How do I close out the day?

ul: Agenda → Tasks. Anything due today or overdue in amber.
New mail / chat still unread? Open the thread — opening it marks mail read.
Leave a note on the ticket or meeting if tomorrow-you will not remember the call.
Do not rely on chat history for promises. A task or a note on the card is the record.

items.h: How do I pick a time with an offshore team?

ul: Click the digital clock above Desk chat.
Add their city (search is typo-tolerant). You stay on the You row.
Hover a column. Click two hours to mark a window.
Propose that window in mail — the desk will not send a calendar invite.

blocks.p: “What’s a good time next week for #ACME SSO with the India team?” It suggests windows from past meetings and locations. It does not create the event.

items.h: How do I see today on Agenda?

ul: Day / Week / Month at the top.
Arrows change the day. The red line is Now.
A meeting card shows the company logo on the left and duration minutes on the right.
Newest first. Filter is one control: To (Me / Us / Them / All / ??, multi), type (Email / Slack / Teams / Tasks, multi), From, and when (Today / Yesterday / Last 7 days / custom range).
Far right of a row is who it is to: Me / Us / Them / All / ?? / n/a.
+ creates a task — a mail to yourself. Subject is Tasks: Company : name {type}.

Refresh (next to Agenda / Companies) one-shots Gmail and Calendar for new, changed, and cancelled rows. The desk also does that on a timer (default every 5 minutes per company; shortest interval wins). Checkpoints stay in Couchbase Lite — not a standing Google connection.

items.h: What does Me / Us / Them mean on a row?

blocks.p: That stamp is who the mail or chat is to, from your point of view. It is not stored on the message.

ul: Me — To you (your operator email).
Us — To your side (your domain, account team).
Them — To the customer.
All — mixed To/Cc, or a Slack/Teams channel.
?? — the desk could not tell. n/a — does not apply (a task to yourself).

items.h: How do I filter Agenda to one project?

ul: On Agenda, the Company : Project control (next to Filter).
Pick a book, or a book:project such as ACME:SSO hardening.
Inbox rows with that project_id stay. Meetings for the day still show; the filter is for mail / chat / tasks.
Set it back to All (or Company : Project) to see every book again.

items.h: How do I see next week or the whole month?

ul: Agenda → Week or Month (next to Day).
Arrows walk by week or by month. Click a day on Month to open that Day.
User Preferences can hide Saturday and Sunday and set which day the week begins.

items.h: How do I open a customer book?

ul: Home → Companies.
Each tile is one book: health, next meeting, and counts.
Click a tile. The book opens on the left; chat on the right stays scoped to that book.

items.h: How do I see which books are at risk?

ul: Home → Companies. Health words: healthy, watch, at risk, critical.
Filter the board with the search box (name or abbr).
Refresh health (far right) after you close tickets or load seed — scores are computed on this desk.
Quiet on Settings → Companies hides a book from Home without deleting it.

items.h: How do I ask the desk a question?

ul: The right pane is always chat.
On Home it covers the whole desk. With a book open it is only about that account.
On Home, type # to pick a company. Inside a book, skip # — this thread stays on that company.
/people and /ticket bound the question. You can chain them.
@ talks to a person (address / send). Use /people when you mean search for them.
Example: “what was /people bob response to /ticket ACME-12?”

items.h: What do #, @, and / mean in chat?

blocks.p: Same prefixes as book Search. Slash bounds a question. @ addresses a person. # picks a company on Home only.

ul: Type / — bound this question. /people lists people, /ticket lists tickets. Chain: “what was /people bob response to /ticket ACME-12?”
Type @ — talk to that person (a message / address). The menu is people on this book (or every book on Home).
Type # — companies, on Home only. Inside Acme (or any book) chat does not point at another company.
Far left on the open book. Type /people bob to find a person, /ticket ACME-12 for a ticket, /email, /chat, /project.
That is search. @ in chat is talk-to, not search.

items.h: How do I ask a question across every book?

ul: Stay on Home (no book open) so chat is desk-wide.
Ask: “What tasks are due this week?” or “What is on fire at #ACME?”
If it asks which book, type # and pick the company, or open the company first.
History and Bookmark still work. New chat starts a clean thread.

items.h: What do Open, Compose, and Add note do?

blocks.p: Buttons under an assistant bubble run screens you already have. They never send.

ul: Open — jumps to the book, ticket, or thread named in the answer.
Compose — opens the shared mail composer with To / Cc filled when chat proposed them. You still Save draft or Send.
Add note — same Notes block as a timeline card, on this chat thread.
Add person / Update title — opens the people sheet when someone on a chain is missing or their title changed.

items.h: Why didn't chat send the email?

ul: On purpose. Chat drafts; you send.
Use Compose under the bubble, or Compose on the book.
Send in the lightbox asks you to confirm when SMTP is live.
If SMTP is off you get send_not_configured — set it under Settings → connectors.

items.h: How do I find an old desk chat?

ul: History (clock) lists earlier threads. Click one to reopen it.
Bookmark pins the current thread.
New chat starts a clean thread.
Hover an icon for its name.

items.h: How do I search a customer book?

blocks.p: Use the search box at the top of the book (far left). Plain text filters the current tab. Type / to jump type and to find a person.

ul: /people bob — search for that person. Type /people and pick. The people tab opens and filters.
In chat, /people bob bounds the question. @bob is talk-to, not search.
/ticket ACME-12 — tickets
/email outage — mail threads
/chat DC3 — Slack and Teams together
/slack pin or /teams Bob — still the slack / teams tab
/project all — people who own every project
/calendar QBR — meetings
/sf renewal — Salesforce
/note call Pat — notes on timeline events

items.h: How do I read the timeline?

ul: Events run around a Now line.
Horizontal: past on the left, future on the right.
Vertical: newest at the top, oldest at the bottom.
Past 7 / Past 30 and Next 7 / Next 30 bound the window.
Now recenters after you scroll. Click a card for the lightbox.

items.h: How do I leave a note on a ticket or meeting?

ul: Open the timeline card, ticket, thread, or meeting (click the row).
Notes is at the bottom of the lightbox, same as chat Add note.
Type what you would tell tomorrow-you. Save note.
Notes stay on that card. They are not a mail and they are not a Jira comment.

items.h: How do I compose or reply?

blocks.p: Compose, thread Reply, and New task share one mail composer.

ul: To / Cc / Bcc are Tagify chips — pick people, do not type a raw list.
Attach files, then AI Suggest, Save draft, or Send (far right).
Send asks you to confirm when SMTP is live. If SMTP is off you get send_not_configured.

items.h: How do I mark mail as read?

ul: Open the thread on email or from Agenda. Opening it marks the thread read.
Agenda New mail only lists unread mail (tasks still show even if you opened them).
There is no separate “mark unread” control on the row yet.

items.h: How do I read Slack and Teams for one book?

ul: Open the book → slack / teams (one tab).
Search /chat, /slack, or /teams plus a word or person.
Agenda also lists unread Slack and Teams with an All stamp on channels.
Pins and unread live on the message. This desk does not post back to Slack or Teams.

items.h: How do I see Salesforce on a book?

ul: Open the book → Salesforce.
Opportunities and cases that already synced to this book.
Search /sf renewal or /sf case.
This is a view of what is here — it does not edit Salesforce.

items.h: How do I find a meeting on the book calendar?

ul: Open the book → calendar, or click the card on Home Agenda.
Search /calendar QBR on the book.
Home Agenda is your day across every book. The book calendar is that company only.

items.h: How do I put mail or a ticket on a project?

ul: Open the timeline (or mail / ticket) card.
Assign a project on that card.
That is how mail, tickets, Slack, Teams, and Salesforce land on the right book of work.

items.h: How do I see who is on a project?

ul: Open people. Search the project name, or type /people in book Search to pick a person.
Org chart and Account team are the same people, different views.
Directors who own every project: check All projects, or type /project all.

items.h: How do I add a person from an email chain?

ul: Open the book → people → Add person (far right).
Email is the key. Name, title, Reports to, Projects, and Functions are Tagify or search-select.
In chat or book Search, @bob finds someone already on People. Add person is for a new email that is not on the book yet.
If chat names someone not on People, use Add person under the bubble — it seeds the email.
Update title when a signature shows a new role for someone already on the book.

items.h: How do I see who reports to whom?

ul: Open the book → org chart (customer) or account team (your side).
Reports to on Add / Edit person builds the tree. Do not point at another company.
People is the flat list if you only need search.

items.h: How do I add or edit a project?

ul: Open projects. Search or filter by type and status.
Add project: type, status, owner from people, optional group email, tags (type and press Enter).
Click a row to edit. Remove asks you to type the project name — Cancel if you clicked by mistake.

items.h: How do I tag someone Ops or Accounting?

blocks.p: On People, Add or Edit person. Functions is a Tagify field — Ops, Accounting, DBA, or your own label. Search finds those chips.

items.h: How do I compare timezones?

ul: Click the digital clock above Desk chat.
Search a city (Los Angeles, even “las angoles”).
Add or remove rows. Drag the handle to reorder.
Hover a column to compare. A red * on the You row means that hour is already on your calendar.
Click an hour to list your meetings then. Click a second hour to check a window.
Your timezone is the You row. Picks survive refresh.

items.h: How do I see if a time is already booked?

ul: Open World clock from the digital clock.
On the You row, a red * under am/pm means that hour has a meeting.
Click the hour — meetings for that slot list at the bottom, not the timezone conversion line.
Click a second hour to see everything in that window. The desk does not create a calendar event from the clock.

items.h: How does AI know how I work?

blocks.p: AI has no guess of whether you are selling, owning the relationship, or working a ticket. Settings → You is that guidance.

ul: Sales / account executive — account-level, is the team helping, openings to sell or upsell only when the book supports it.
Technical Account Manager — more ticket and people detail, blockers, owners.
Customer Success Manager — health, next actions, who owes whom.
Support / escalation — the issue, who is waiting, no pitch.
Write your own — blank intent. Describe altitude, tone, and what to lead with.
The textarea is what the model actually reads. Edit the preset. Save profile.
It flavors chat, compose, task assist, and weekly report. It does not invent tickets or pipeline.

items.h: How do I set who I am?

ul: Settings → You: name, phone, email, timezone.
How you work: pick a persona (CSM, sales, TAM, support) then edit Intent and style. Save profile.
That text is injected into every AI chat and draft so a sales rep gets account-level answers and a TAM gets more ticket detail.
Mail from your domain is treated as internal, not a customer book.
Timezone pins You on the world clock and drives Agenda’s idea of today.

items.h: How do I hide weekends or switch night mode?

ul: Settings → User Preferences.
Uncheck Saturday and Sunday for a weekday grid. Pick which day the week begins.
Appearance: Day, Night, or Auto.
The sun and moon at the bottom of the sidebar also switches Day and Night.

items.h: How do I add a customer book?

ul: Settings → Companies → Add company.
Quiet hides it from Home. Remove archives it — type the abbreviation (ACME) in the confirm sheet.
Edit: color, crop a logo, domains, Slack / Teams / Salesforce / Jira tags so inbound mail lands on the right book.

items.h: How do I connect mail, chat, and AI?

ul: Gmail and Calendar: save your profile email, then Sign in with Google.
Jira: site + API token. Slack: xoxp token. Teams: Connect Microsoft.
To send mail or a task, set SMTP (host, port, username, app password). Send always asks first.
Okta SSO still needs an OIDC app client ID.

items.h: How do I load lab data?

ul: Settings → Lab → Load seed data.
Three books: ACME (navy), NWIN (forest), GLX (burgundy), each with people, tickets, mail, chat, and a realistic meeting day.
Seed is safe to run again. Reset wipes books and keeps your settings, including the world clock.
